The absolute-trend gate (eligible=true) is the one validated risk-control leg, so holding it is defensible. I lean overweight on trend continuation, not on momentum alpha. The rotation is broad and non-directional (directional=false), so leadership is fragile.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the rotation challenger (rank 2, score 1.11) and is eligible through the absolute-trend gate. It is uncrowded (z=0.20) and in a broad-rotation regime where the leader is crowded, so a second trend-following leg in gold offers non-correlated commodity leadership exposure. This is a trend-following lean, not a momentum-return claim; momentum rank is only a focus lens. Low conviction because breadth is narrow (0.267) and durability is middling (0.48).
theses.dissent: Gold breadth is thin (0.267) and its durability tag is 'mixed', so the trend is not confirmed as persistent; if the prevailing market-level narrative (dominant: 'markets', 'geopolitics') shifts to risk-on, gold miners can lag energy and financials for weeks. Mean-reversion tendencies in precious metals sub-sectors are a headwind.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks rank 5 (score 0.423, eligible=true) with a 'trend' hurst_tag and durability 0.59 — the strongest trend-quality signal among eligible themes — and no crowding (z=-0.01). Not a momentum call; Big Banks are the cleanest trend-following candidate outside the crowded energy/pockets complex.
